q: If f(n) = 3n² + 5n + 2, which of the following is correct?
exp: Dominant term is 3n², so f(n) is bounded above and below by constant multiples of n²: Θ(n²).

q: The solution of the recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n with T(1) = 1 is
exp: Master theorem: a=2, b=2, n^(log₂2) = n equals f(n), so T(n) = Θ(n log n).

q: What is the maximum number of comparisons needed to merge two sorted lists of sizes m and n into one sorted list?
exp: Each comparison outputs one element; the last element is placed without comparison, so at most m + n − 1 comparisons.

What is the length of a longest common subsequence of X = ABCBDAB and Y = BDCABA?
exp: One LCS is BCBA (also BDAB); no common subsequence of length 5 exists, so the length is 4.

q: How many distinct solutions does the 6-queens problem have?
exp: The 6×6 board admits exactly 4 non-attacking arrangements of 6 queens.

q: Strassen's matrix multiplication algorithm multiplies two n × n matrices in time
exp: Strassen uses 7 recursive multiplications: T(n) = 7T(n/2) + Θ(n²) = Θ(n^log₂7).

q: In a graph with edges A-B (4), A-C (1), C-B (2), B-D (1), C-D (5), D-E (3), the shortest distance from A to E, found by Dijkstra's algorithm, is
exp: Distances: C=1, B=min(4,1+2)=3, D=min(3+1,1+5)=4, E=4+3=7 via A-C-B-D-E.

q: The Held-Karp dynamic programming algorithm solves the Travelling Salesman Problem for n cities in time
exp: There are n·2ⁿ subproblems (subset, last city) each taking O(n) to compute, giving O(n² 2ⁿ).

q: Which of the following decision problems is NP-complete?
options: Single-source shortest path with non-negative weights
Searching a key in a sorted array
exp: Hamiltonian cycle is a classic NP-complete problem; the others are solvable in polynomial time.

q: For the pattern 'abcabcab', the last entry of the KMP prefix (failure) function is
exp: The longest proper prefix of 'abcabcab' that is also a suffix is 'abcab', of length 5.

q: For quick sort that always uses the first element as pivot, which input gives the worst case O(n²)?
options: An array already sorted in ascending order
An array in which every partition splits into equal halves
A randomly shuffled array of distinct keys
An array in which the first element is always the median of its subarray
exp: With sorted input the first element is the minimum, so partitions are of size 0 and n−1 each time, giving T(n) = T(n−1) + n.

q: The solution of T(n) = 4T(n/2) + n² is
exp: a=4, b=2, n^(log₂4) = n² matches f(n) = n², case 2 gives Θ(n² log n).

q: Edges of a graph: A-B 2, B-C 3, A-C 4, C-D 1, B-D 5, D-E 6, C-E 7. The weight of a minimum spanning tree found by Kruskal's algorithm is
exp: Pick C-D 1, A-B 2, B-C 3, skip A-C and B-D (cycles), pick D-E 6: total 12.

q: A 0/1 knapsack has capacity 7 and items (weight, value): (1,1), (3,4), (4,5), (5,7). The maximum total value is
exp: Best feasible subsets: {3,4} gives 4+5 = 9; {1,5} gives 8; {5} gives 7. Maximum is 9.

q: What is the maximum number of element comparisons binary search makes on a sorted array of 1000 elements (successful or unsuccessful)?
In branch and bound for a minimisation problem, a live node is pruned when
options: its lower bound is less than the best cost found so far
it is a leaf node of the state space tree
its lower bound is greater than or equal to the cost of the best solution found so far
it has more than two children
exp: If even the optimistic estimate cannot beat the current best, the subtree cannot contain a better solution.

q: Which of the following lists the functions in increasing order of growth rate?
exp: Polynomial functions grow slower than exponential, and n! grows faster than 2ⁿ.

q: Jobs with (deadline, profit): J1 (2,100), J2 (1,19), J3 (2,27), J4 (1,25), J5 (3,15). Each job takes unit time. The maximum profit obtainable by greedy job sequencing is
exp: Sorted by profit: J1 takes slot 2, J3 slot 1, J4 and J2 rejected, J5 slot 3. Profit 100+27+15 = 142.

q: The Floyd–Warshall algorithm for all-pairs shortest paths on a graph with n vertices runs in time
exp: Three nested loops over k, i, j each run n times.

q: Matrices A (10×20), B (20×30) and C (30×40) are to be multiplied. The minimum number of scalar multiplications is

In the 4-queens problem, the first queen is placed at row 1, column 1. Scanning columns from left to right, the leftmost safe column for the queen in row 2 is
exp: Column 1 shares the column and column 2 shares the diagonal with the first queen; column 3 is the first safe one.

q: If an NP-complete problem X is shown to be solvable in polynomial time, then
exp: Every NP problem reduces to X in polynomial time, so all of NP would be in P.

q: The fractional knapsack problem has capacity 50 and items (weight, value): (10,60), (20,100), (30,120). The maximum value obtainable is
exp: Ratios 6, 5, 4. Take items 1 and 2 (value 160) and 20/30 of item 3 (value 80): total 240.

In a multistage graph S→{A,B}→{C,D}→T with costs S-A 2, S-B 3, A-C 4, A-D 1, B-C 2, B-D 5, C-T 3, D-T 6, the minimum cost from S to T is
Which of the following statements is NOT true?
exp: (n+1)! = (n+1)·n!, which is not bounded by a constant multiple of n!. The other three hold.

q: For a text of length n and a pattern of length m, the worst-case running time of the naive string matching algorithm is
exp: It tries n−m+1 shifts, each needing up to m character comparisons.

q: The greedy choice of taking items in decreasing order of value-to-weight ratio gives an optimal solution for
exp: Ratio-greedy is optimal only when items can be split.

q: The time complexity of Prim's algorithm using a binary heap and an adjacency list is
exp: Each edge may cause a decrease-key of O(log V), plus V extract-mins.

q: The auxiliary space required by the standard array-based merge sort is
exp: Merging needs a temporary array of size up to n.

q: The matrix chain multiplication problem for n matrices can be solved by dynamic programming in time
exp: There are O(n²) subchains and each considers O(n) split points.

q:
Statement I: Backtracking explores the state space tree in a depth-first manner.
Statement II: Branch and bound is generally applied to optimisation problems.
Which is correct?
options: Both Statement I and II are true
exp: Backtracking uses DFS with feasibility pruning; branch and bound uses bounds to prune in optimisation problems.

q: The first problem proved NP-complete by the Cook–Levin theorem was
exp: Cook (1971) showed SAT is NP-complete; the others were later shown by reductions.

exp: The greedy finalisation of a vertex's distance assumes no later path can be shorter, which fails with negative edges.

q: If quick sort always splits the array in the ratio 9:1, its recurrence T(n) = T(9n/10) + T(n/10) + n has solution
exp: Every level costs at most n and depth is log_(10/9) n, so the total is Θ(n log n).

q: The length of the longest common subsequence of AGGTAB and GXTXAYB is
exp: The LCS is GTAB.

q: The time complexity of the dynamic programming solution to the 0/1 knapsack problem with n items and capacity W is
exp: The table has n × W entries, each computed in O(1); this is pseudo-polynomial.
